URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/1/blasts-heard-in-addis-ababa-as-ethiopia-conflict-widens-in-the-north
Al Jazeera — confirmed published 1 October 2026, 14:25 BST. Headline: "Blasts heard in Addis Ababa as Ethiopia conflict widens in the north"

Explosions occurred overnight in Addis Ababa. According to three diplomatic sources, the blasts happened hours after the government imposed a ban on drone-flying over the city and surrounding areas.

The Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival claimed responsibility. A source linked to the rebel coalition told Reuters that the alliance "had carried out several drone strikes in Addis Ababa, including some targeting the military's headquarters."

The alliance comprises seven armed groups, including the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and groups from multiple regions, and seeks to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government.

Tigray front: government forces have advanced northward to roughly 40km from Mekelle, Tigray's regional capital. The TPLF withdrew fighters to new defensive positions, with some leaders evacuating the city. Thousands of civilians fled fearing clashes. Electricity and internet services were cut in the region.

Eritrea: Ethiopia ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave within 48 hours and announced the closure of its embassy in Asmara, accusing Eritrea of "direct and indirect acts of hostility." Eritrea denies supporting the opposition alliance.

No casualty figures in this article.
